state.label: Multi-Hazard · Active
state.detail: A busy Northern-Hemisphere summer across several hazards at once: a US wildfire season at the highest national readiness level, an above-average severe-convective season, deadly flooding across Asia, and prolonged drought and heat in Europe. Fire and water are the dominant active signals.

narrative: The watchman's read for mid-August is a multi-hazard one. The United States is carrying its most demanding active hazard in wildfire — more than 7.2 million acres burned, 169% of the ten-year average, at Preparedness Level 5 — alongside a severe-convective season running above its ten-year envelope. The wet signal sits over Asia, where record Kanto rainfall and a deadly Indian monsoon are the sharpest flood events, while Europe runs dry under a fifth heatwave. This dashboard is a register of those events: what is active now on the global map, and how the US fire and severe-storm seasons compare with climatology. The broad ocean and El Niño backdrop that ties them together is tracked in the companion ENSO dashboard; here the focus is the events themselves.
